title: Yehudah ben Gedidya

paragraphs: In the time of King Yannai (Yohanan the High Priest), in Kiddushin 66a: Elazar ben Po'eira said to King Yannai, "The hearts of the Pharisees are against you." There was a certain elder there, Yehuda ben Gedidya by name, and he said to King Yannai, "Let the crown of kingship suffice you; leave the crown of priesthood to the seed of Aaron," for they used to say that his mother had been taken captive in Modi'im. The matter was investigated and was not found, and the Sages of Israel departed in anger (that is, they were angry at Yehuda ben Gedidya; we will discuss this at length in the entry Yannai the King).

notes.text: Yannai’s identification as Yohanan and the parenthetical interpretation that the sages were angry at Gedidya are Hyman’s own comments. The accusation about Yannai’s mother remains unsubstantiated in the account.

The inspected Kiddushin 66a explicitly reports the unsubstantiated accusation and the sages’ departure in anger. The supplied Yohanan identification and the interpretation that they were angry at Gedidya remain Hyman’s comments.
